test_title: SSC Selection Post 2024 (Matriculation Level) Official Paper (Held On: 21 Jun, 2024 Shift 4)
subject: general
question: Who has the power to prorogue the House or either House of State Legislature from time to time?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The power to prorogue the House or either House of the State Legislature from time to time is vested in the **Governor**.
 
• This power is part of the Governor's broader role in the legislative process, which includes summoning and dissolving the state legislative assembly.
 
• The Governor acts on the advice of the state's Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers but retains certain discretionary powers.
 
• The ability to prorogue the legislature helps in managing the legislative calendar and addressing situations where the House may need to be temporarily suspended.
 
• Proroguing the House effectively ends a session but does not dissolve the legislative assembly, allowing for the continuation of the legislative process in the future.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Governor** is appointed by the President of India and acts as the central government's representative in the state.
 
• The Governor's role is outlined in the **Constitution of India**, particularly in Articles 153 to 167.
 
• The Governor has both executive and legislative powers, including giving assent to bills passed by the state legislature, issuing ordinances, and making recommendations for President's Rule in the state.
 
• In addition to proroguing the House, the Governor can also dissolve the legislative assembly, usually upon the advice of the Chief Minister.
 
• The **Governor** plays a crucial role in maintaining the constitutional framework and ensuring the smooth functioning of the state government.
